observations.limitation: Verbose logs truncate configs, specialization_data and key. Exact distinct specialization cannot be recovered from retained text; no assertion about which scalar/alignment class was missing.
observations.conditioning_matches_scope: Four same-time conditioning log entries; both measured entries exactly match a visible conditioning compile-details string. This does not identify complete specialization keys.

source_findings: fused_moe.py:297-345 is a plain @triton.jit kernel, with runtime N/K/EM/num_valid_tokens and strides plus constexpr tiling/routing flags. invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel:820-909 derives launch dimensions/strides from actual tensors. No JIT warmup-provider registration found in this kernel file or triton_moe.py.

kernel_warmup.py:172-198 calls registry.warmup for explicitly registered providers, plus specialized model warmups. Logs show89 keys/5 kernels, not exhaustive full-model MoE dispatch coverage. BF16 router GEMM warmup at98 is router projection, not expert fused_moe_kernel.
jit_warmup.py:1050-1085 registers providers only under active registry and expands their declared keys. A plain Triton JIT kernel does not automatically enumerate runtime signature classes.

fused_moe.py:1427-1442 selects nearest tuned config based on runtime token count M. Equal request concurrency does not guarantee identical scheduled token counts, prefill/decode mixes, intermediate tensor strides or Triton scalar-specialization classes.

jit_monitor.py:144-151 truncates repr to120 chars; 201-229 applies that to config/specialization data and key. Therefore the two new events can have identical visible metadata despite distinct underlying keys.
candidate_improvement: Implement an owner-backed compile-only warmup provider for BF16 Triton expert GEMMs using actual layer dimensions/strides/top-k and the same runtime config resolver. Enumerate reachable tiling configs and Triton scalar/alignment signature classes for both up/gate and down projections. First add complete stable specialization-key digest to diagnostic output to identify missing classes. Do not simply repeat the same concurrency warmup or assume router warmup covers expert GEMMs. This is a source-supported direction, not a validated implementation.
